extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, and KIPO examiners (Korea)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examiner guidance for filing, examining, and deciding applications to register patent term extensions due to delayed registration under the Korean Patent Act (Articles 92-2—92-5 and relevant Enforcement Rules). Covers required contents, documents, timing, amendment rules, calculation of allowable extension, notices, decisions, publication, and appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of application (Article 92-3(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for registration of patent term extension shall state: 1) the name and domicile of the applicant for registration of extension (or corporate name and business office), 2) the name and domicile (or business office) of an agent, if any (and firm name and designated patent attorney where applicable), 3) the number of the patent whose term is subject to extension, 4) the period of application for extension, and 5) grounds for extension prescribed by Ordinance (with substantiating materials attached).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All five items must be included in the written application; supporting evidential documents for the stated grounds must be attached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing deadline (Article 92-3(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for registration of patent term extension must be filed within three months from the date of registration of the patent right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed before the patent is registered or after the three-month period has elapsed, the examiner shall give an opportunity for explanation under the Enforcement Rules and return the application to the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility and joint ownership (Article 92-3(3), 4.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only a patent right holder may be an applicant for registration of extension. Where a patent right is jointly owned, an application must be filed by all joint owners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application filed by a person who is not the patent right holder, or by an incomplete set of co-owners, constitutes a ground for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required form and attachments (Enforcement Rules Article 54-2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must use the prescribed written application form (Annexed Form 30-2 / Annexed Form 30 as applicable) and attach: 1) the ground for extension and a copy of evidential documents, and 2) a power of attorney where a representative conducts the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to use the correct form or to attach required evidentiary documents/power of attorney will be treated as a formality violation and may lead to an amendment order or return/invalidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for extension / eligibility criteria (Article 54-3; Article 92-3(1)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounds designated by Ordinance include: (1) a need to extend the patent term because the patent was registered after four years from the filing date or three years from the date of request for examination, whichever is later; (2) a specification of the period of request for extension and an explanation that the period of delay attributable to the applicant is reduced (with evidential document); and (3) other necessary items to prove the ground for extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application must explain and document the relevant delay periods and any reductions in applicant-attributable delay; evidential documents must be attached for each claimed ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formality examination and examiner remedies (5.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application transferred from document-receipt is in violation of formalities, the examiner shall: (1) indicate intention to return with grounds and a period for explanation where filing deadline under Article 92-3(2) has elapsed; (2) order amendment where provisions re: representation, fee payment, or other formalities are violated; and (3) invalidate the proceeding (in name of Commissioner) if irregularities are not addressed within the designated period despite amendment orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifications of return or amendment must state the ground and allow an opportunity for explanation; return or invalidation follow if defects persist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of subject for substantive examination (5.4.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The subject for examination is the application to register the patent term extension and its attached documents. When amendments are made, the examiner must decide whether to permit them; legitimate amendments are reflected in the subject for examination, illegitimate amendments are deemed never made, and where multiple amendments occur, the examiner uses the combination of the finally-amended parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If amendments are legitimate, the application is examined as amended; if not legitimate, the pre-amendment application is examined. Refer to the chapter 'Determination Standard of Amended Content' for multi-amendment situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory grounds for rejection (Article 92-4)
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner shall decide to reject the application where: 1) the length of extension requested exceeds the period recognized under Article 92-2; 2) the applicant is not the patentee; or 3) the application is filed in violation of Article 92-3(3) (e.g., joint owner filing requirement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any of these statutory grounds apply the examiner issues notice of ground for rejection and proceeds under the applicable examination provisions (mutatis mutandis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation method for allowable extension period (5.4.2, ①–⑤)
rubrics_metrics.description: The allowable extension period is computed as: (③) the number of days (E) from the reference date (C) — the later of four years from filing (A) or three years from request for examination (B) — to the date of establishment of the patent right after patent fee payment (D), minus (④) the total period of delay attributable to the applicant (F) (sum of periods under Article 7-2(1) and related provisions, accounting for overlaps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps include: ① determine the filing date for calculation (special rules for divisional/converted/international applications etc.); ② pick the later reference date between 4 years from filing and 3 years after examination request; ③ calculate total delay (E) to grant date after fee payment; ④ sum applicant-attributable delay periods, not exceeding actual delay, and account for overlaps; ⑤ subtract applicant delay from total delay to get allowable extension. If the requested period written in the application exceeds this allowable period the examiner notifies a ground for rejection and allows written argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions to applicant-attributable delay (5.4.2④)
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if a period falls under categories of applicant-attributable delay, an objectively-recognized ground showing the delay is not attributable to the applicant will exempt that period from reduction. Examples: when the delay happened before an applicant requested examination; when amendment orders or notices of grounds for rejection were made due to mistakes by KIPO or a patent court; natural disasters; or other non-applicant-caused delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should submit evidential documents to prove such exemptions; examiners may accept and exclude these periods when computing applicant-attributable delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of ground for rejection and written-argument period (5.4.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an examiner intends to reject, he/she shall notify the ground for rejection precisely and concisely so the applicant clearly understands it. At the notice of ground for rejection, the period for submission of a written argument shall be within two months, and this period is extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant may request extension of the written-argument period up to four times for one month each (see extension provisions). The notice must cite the relevant provisions/grounds so the applicant can prepare a response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of written arguments and amendments (5.4.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may submit a written argument or an amendment after notice of ground for rejection; written arguments may be submitted within the designated period and are accepted even if late or submitted before the notice. Amendments can be submitted until a certified copy of the decision to register is delivered, but after a notice of ground for rejection, amendments are allowed only within the written-argument period. Amendable parts under Article 92-3(4) are limited to: (i) the period of request for extension and (ii) the ground for extension designated in Ordinance; changes to the applicant or patent number are not allowed (except correcting clerical errors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an amendment is illegitimate the examiner issues a preliminary notice of inadmissible amendment and gives an opportunity for explanation; if the amendment is not accepted after explanation the examiner re-examines the pre-amendment application and may issue a notification of inadmissible amendment or a decision to reject. If an amendment is recognized as legitimate, the amended application is treated as having been filed originally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision content, transmittal and publication (5.4.5 & 6.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A written decision to register or to reject registration for extension must include: 1) application number of registration of extension, 2) patent number, 3) period for extension, 4) content of period of delay, 5) name and address of applicant, 6) representative's name and address if present, 7) order and ground for decision, and 8) date of decision. When registration is decided, the Commissioner shall serve a certified copy of the decision and request publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A decision to reject shall not contain items 3 and 4. When registration is made, the Registration Division publishes on the Patent Gazette: the name and address of the patentee, the patent number, the date when the patent term extension is registered, and the period of extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal and invalidation remedies (6.2 & 6.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who receives a decision to reject registration for extension may submit a notice of appeal trial within thirty days from the date of transmittal of the certified copy of that decision. Where a patent right whose term was extended falls under any paragraph of Article 134-2, an interested party can request an invalidation trial of the patent right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely filing of the appeal notice is required (30 days from transmittal); invalidation trials are available post-registration under specified statutory grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation rules and scope (4.5 and Article 54-2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing an application to register patent term extension due to delayed registration does not require a special authorization and can be carried out without special authorization. However, where a representative conducts the proceeding a power of attorney must be attached (per Enforcement Rules). The scope of representation may be ambiguous in some cases — reference is made to the manual section on representation for details. Corrections to applicant names (e.g., clerical error) and universal succession name changes are recognized; amendments that would change the patent number are generally not allowed except to correct clerical errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should consult the referenced representation chapter for permitted scope; when represented, ensure power of attorney is attached and that prohibited changes (like patent number) are not attempted beyond clerical correction.
